# Project 1: Drone Visual-Inertial Navigation Pipeline

Project 1 is the main implementation project for the first part of the course. You will build a complete visual-inertial navigation pipeline around a real quadrotor dataset, starting from raw packets and ending with fused navigation estimates and an engineering report you can defend. This project is divided into three staged checkpoints, each building on the previous one. These three parts are not three unrelated mini-projects. They are staged build steps within one end-to-end system. Part A establishes the inertial propagation backbone, Part B builds the visual observation model that corrects it, and Part C fuses both into three nonlinear estimators that you will compare honestly. 

You can find the individual checkpoints here:

- [Project 1a: IMU Dead Reckoning](m1-drone-pipeline-a.qmd)
- [Project 1b: PnP Observation Model](m1-drone-pipeline-b.qmd)
- [Project 1c: EKF, UKF, and Particle Filters](m1-drone-pipeline-c.qmd)

## Project summary

This is the main implementation project for the first part of the course. You will build a complete visual-inertial navigation pipeline around a real quadrotor dataset, starting from raw packets and ending with fused navigation estimates and an engineering report you can defend.

The full workflow is:

``` text
raw drone packets
    -> dataset loading and time alignment
    -> IMU forward propagation
    -> AprilTag-based visual pose estimation
    -> covariance estimation and tuning
    -> EKF / UKF / particle-filter fusion
    -> evaluation against truth
    -> technical report and analysis
```

The three project checkpoints are not three unrelated mini-projects. They are staged build steps within one end-to-end system. Part A establishes the inertial propagation backbone, Part B builds the visual observation model that corrects it, and Part C fuses both into three nonlinear estimators that you will compare honestly.

The main engineering goals are:

- correctness of the math and implementation
- consistent frame and state conventions
- uncertainty modeling that is explicit rather than guessed
- evaluation that compares mechanization, visual observations, and fused estimates against truth

The goal is not to collect a folder full of plausible-looking plots. The goal is to build a pipeline whose assumptions, interfaces, uncertainty models, and failure modes you can explain without hand waving.

Project 1 is worth **50% of the course grade**. It is divided into three staged checkpoints:

+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Checkpoint                        | Focus                                                                  |
+===================================+========================================================================+
| Project 1a                        | IMU forward mechanization and dead reckoning                           |
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Project 1b                        | AprilTag map geometry, PnP pose estimation, and observation covariance |
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Project 1c                        | EKF, UKF, and particle-filter fusion                                   |
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

## Project Architecture

``` text
drone dataset packets
        |
        v
load_drone_dataset(...)
        |
        +--> IMU mechanization / dead reckoning
        |
        +--> AprilTag map + solvePnP pose observations
        |
        v
shared state and uncertainty model
        |
        v
EKF / UKF / particle filter
        |
        v
trajectory, diagnostics, comparison, report
```

All three checkpoints reuse the same dataset, the same timing conventions, and the same shared state definition. If those interfaces drift between Parts A, B, and C, you are no longer building one navigation pipeline. You are building three incompatible experiments.

## Shared Dataset

Download the data once from the repository root (about 570 MB):

``` bash
uv run python scripts/fetch_data.py drone-data
```

This places the following files in `data/drone-data/`:

- `studentdata0.mat` through `studentdata7.mat`
- `parameters.txt`

Load a dataset by index (or pass a file path):

``` python
from drone_pipeline.datasets import load_drone_dataset

dataset = load_drone_dataset(1)  # data/drone-data/studentdata1.mat
```

Each dataset contains:

+-----------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Name                              | Meaning                                                             |
+===================================+=====================================================================+
| `vicon`                           | `12 x N` ground-truth reference sampled at about 100 Hz             |
+-----------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `time`                            | Vicon timestamps in seconds                                         |
+-----------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `data`                            | sensor packets containing images, IMU signals, and tag observations |
+-----------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+

Interpret the Vicon rows as:

|   Rows | Quantity                       |
|-------:|--------------------------------|
|  `0:3` | position `[px, py, pz]`        |
|  `3:6` | roll, pitch, yaw               |
|  `6:9` | linear velocity `[vx, vy, vz]` |
| `9:12` | angular velocity               |

Each packet contains:

+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Field                  | Meaning                                        |
+========================+================================================+
| `img`                  | grayscale camera image                         |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `id`                   | AprilTag IDs observed in the image             |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `p1`, `p2`, `p3`, `p4` | detected pixel coordinates for each tag corner |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `t`                    | packet timestamp in seconds                    |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `rpy`                  | onboard roll-pitch-yaw estimate                |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `drpy`                 | body angular-rate input                        |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| `acc`                  | body-frame accelerometer input                 |
+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+

Some packets contain no visible tags. That is normal. Your filter and observation pipeline must skip missing visual measurements cleanly rather than treating them as a software emergency.

## Shared State and Measurement Convention

Use this 15-state vector throughout Parts A, B, and C:

``` python
x = [
    px, py, pz,
    roll, pitch, yaw,
    vx, vy, vz,
    bgx, bgy, bgz,
    bax, bay, baz,
]
```

Use the roll-pitch-yaw rotation convention:

``` python
R_world_body = Rz(yaw) @ Ry(pitch) @ Rx(roll)
```

All angles must be in radians. Whenever you subtract two attitudes, wrap the residual into `[-pi, pi)`. If you do not, the filter will eventually produce very confident nonsense near angle discontinuities.

The visual measurement used in Parts B and C is:

``` python
z = [px, py, pz, roll, pitch, yaw]
```

So the nominal measurement model in Part C is:

``` python
h(x) = x[:6]
```

## Starter Package Layout

You are expected to work from the standardized starter package in `projects/drone_pipeline/` rather than building the project as a single notebook or one very large script.

Relevant starter interfaces:

``` python
from drone_pipeline.datasets import (
    interpolate_vicon_truth,
    load_drone_dataset,
    load_drone_parameters,
)
from drone_pipeline.observation import (
    build_apriltag_corner_map,
    estimate_measurement_covariance,
    estimate_pose,
)
from drone_pipeline.mechanization import propagate_state
from drone_pipeline.filters import (
    EKFNavigator,
    ParticleFilterNavigator,
    UKFNavigator,
)
```

You may add helper modules, notebooks, and analysis scripts, but keep your public project interfaces stable and keep the code organized enough that another engineer can run and inspect it without reverse-engineering your folder habits.

## Truth Usage Rules

The `vicon` data is the truth reference.

You may use it to:

- evaluate error
- estimate measurement covariance
- study drift and consistency
- compare filters

You may not use it as a recurring measurement inside the navigation solution itself. If your filter is secretly using Vicon as an update, that is not visual-inertial navigation. That is expensive cheating.

## Development Split

Unless you justify another split, use:

- development and tuning: `studentdata0.mat` through `studentdata4.mat`
- validation and reporting: `studentdata5.mat` through `studentdata7.mat`

You are trying to build a pipeline that generalizes, not one that was hand-tuned until it wins a beauty contest on one file.
